title: Epochless transient-forwarding KV compaction and decode-coalescing policy for low-latency paged-attention
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Investigate and prototype an 'epochless' KV compaction strategy combined with a transient-forwarding reservation and decode-coalescing scheduling policy to reduce prefill-induced stalls and eviction churn in paged attention workloads. The goal is to minimize tail decode latency and reduce unnecessary kernel churn while keeping memory reclamation low-overhead and tenant-friendly.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implemented in runtime dev branch with flags: --transient-forwarding and --decode-coalesce
End-to-end integration test showing P99 decode latency improvement of >= 25% on the conversational prefix workload compared to baseline (current prefill + LRU) under mixed tenant load
Prefill stall frequency reduced by >= 30% on our synthetic multi-session benchmark (50% long context workloads)
No regression in memory safety or incorrect KV hits (unit and fuzz tests pass)
Documented performance trade-offs and a rollout plan in Confluence with rollback hooks and observability dashboards
work_items: Design doc: describe transient-forwarding reservation (lightweight shadow reservation adjacent to target slab) and decode-coalescing wave grouping; add kernel hint API for 'sticky-kernel' and 'coalesce-window'
Prototype transient-forwarding allocator in runtime: shadow reservations borrowed from neighbor slabs for 10-40ms windows; implement admission control to avoid cross-tenant starvation
Add decode-coalescing scheduler: group incoming prefill/decodes into micro-waves by affinity (kernel/cuda context) with max delay cap of 6ms
Integrate simple epochless compaction pass: opportunistic compaction triggered when free-space below threshold and no active decode waves touching page

Benchmarks: create reproducible harness with mixed short/long context traces and multi-tenant weightings; run baseline and new policy across GPU types (A100/H100) and report token/sec and tail latency
PR: submit incremental PRs for allocator, scheduler, and compaction; link to load tests and flame graphs
Console dashboards: add new panels for prefill-stall-rate, transient-forwarding-admissions, coalesce-delay, and kernel-switches/sec
Safety review: coordinate with Security/Infra for cross-tenant borrowing policy and eviction visibility
decisions: Use 'epochless' compaction (opportunistic lightweight passes) instead of synchronous global GC epochs to avoid stop-the-world stalls
Transient-forwarding uses timeboxed shadow reservations (default 25ms) to absorb short-lived prefill spikes and reduce immediate evictions
Decode-coalescing groups affinity-aligned prefill operations up to a 6ms cap to reduce kernel switches; if cap exceeded, group flushes to avoid head-of-line blocking
Admission control favors same-tenant reservation reuse for fairness; cross-tenant forwarding allowed only under low contention with global cap
We expose knobs: coalesce_window_ms, transient_ttl_ms, forwarding_cross_tenant_limit to operations via config and Console
risks: Cross-tenant transient forwarding could cause noisy-neighbor memory pressure if not tightly bounded
Coalescing delay trade-off may increase median latency slightly for the benefit of tail improvements; must tune default window
Opportunistic compaction might increase CPU utilization on control plane nodes if not rate-limited
Incorrect kernel hinting could lead to suboptimal kernel selection and increased decode time; need robust fallbacks
Complexity increases attack surface for bugs in allocator logic—requires thorough unit + property tests
metrics: Target: P99 decode latency -25% vs baseline on conv-prefix workload
Target: prefill-stall-rate -30% on synthetic mixed workload
Target: kernel-switches/sec reduced by >= 40% (measured per-GPU) for grouped waves
Memory reclamation latency (time-to-free after eviction signal) <= 12ms on average
No increase in overall token-cost by >5% when coalescing enabled
notes: Background: current LRU + immediate-evict-on-prefill causes oscillation under bursty long-context traffic; many existing tickets optimize eviction heuristics but introduce GC epochs or large compaction passes (see related issues)

Transient-forwarding idea: allocate a tiny 'forwarding' hold in an adjacent slab that can be returned quickly; during a prefill, if target slab is full and eviction would be expensive, write into forwarding hold and schedule an async gentle compaction to reconcile
Decode-coalescing: leverage kernel affinity information (attention kernel variants) to batch prefills/decodes that would otherwise trigger kernel switching; reduces cuda context thrash
Kernel hint API: lightweight tag in rpc header to indicate 'prefer-current-kernel' or 'can-requeue-for-coalesce'
Fallbacks: if forwarding capacity exhausted, fall back to baseline immediate eviction; if coalesce windows exceed threshold, priority bursts can bypass coalescer
Integration points: allocator changes in runtime/kv/slot_allocator.cc; scheduler in runtime/decode/scheduler.cc; unit tests under runtime/tests/kv_forwarding_test.cc
